selectedDefects.issueTitle: "Properties" -> "Plugin Data" -> "Remove" button enabled on first show with no rows selected
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the observable is a QPushButton enabled state that must track a QItemSelectionModel on a QTableView. The affected build computes removeCustomDataButton->setEnabled(!m_customData->isEmpty()), the fixed build computes it from customDataTable->selectionModel()->hasSelection(). Reading it means walking a real QWidget tree over AT-SPI, finding the push button by its accessible name inside the entry Properties page, and reading the enabled state before any row is clicked, then clicking a table row and reading it again. That is a model/view row state and widget enablement path, not a DOM assertion, and the neighbouring legal behaviour (button enabled after selecting a row) is observable through the same channel

toolkitEvidence.proof: set(QT_COMPONENTS Core Network Concurrent Gui Svg Widgets Test LinguistTools) followed by find_package(Qt5 COMPONENTS ${QT_COMPONENTS} DBus REQUIRED) at line 518; src/CMakeLists.txt links Qt5::Widgets and the tree carries no Quick or Qml component

remaining: build a headless x86_64 Linux image with Qt5 Widgets, Xvfb and AT-SPI, and compile the application at both revisions
author a minimized trigger: open a database fixture that has an entry carrying custom data, open the entry editor Properties page, read the Remove button enabled state before any selection
author the neighbouring legal check: click a plugin data row and confirm the button becomes enabled on both revisions, proving the harness can select rows
run three affected reproductions and three fixed controls and record the evidence pair

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Password generator skips special characters when using AutoGeneratePasswordForNewEntries=true
selectedDefects.whySuitable: a persisted-settings restore across a widget lifecycle rather than an input path, so it exercises a different part of the adapter than the selection defect. The saved generator configuration is written from the password generator widget, and the observable is the text that EditEntryWidget places into the entry password QLineEdit when a new entry is created. Reading it means driving the settings widget, closing it, opening the new entry dialog and reading the line edit contents back through the accessibility text interface; the affected build produces a password drawn from the default character classes, the fixed build honours the stored length and character classes

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the observable is the checked state, and the enabled state, of QCheckBox widgets on the Browser Integration page of the entry editor when a group above the entry overrides the option. selectedDefects.issueTitle: qView window gets unmaximized after exiting full screen
selectedDefects.whySuitable: a window state restore across a QMainWindow lifecycle. MainWindow::toggleFullScreen restores storedWindowState and then, on the affected revision only, calls setWindowSize(), which resizes the window to the image and destroys the restored maximized state. The observable is the top level window state and geometry read back after the fullscreen round trip, which is exactly what the Qt Widgets adapter must be able to see and drive: send the fullscreen toggle as a key to the widget, wait for the window state change, read maximized back. An independent second application from keepassxc, and a window level observable rather than an in-dialog one

toolkitEvidence.proof: QT += core gui network widgets; the repository tree at that revision has no CMakeLists.txt and no qml directory, and the changed file src/mainwindow.cpp is a QMainWindow subclass

remaining: build both revisions with qmake and Qt5 Widgets in the headless image
confirm the window manager in the container honours maximize and fullscreen; a bare Xvfb with no WM will not, so a lightweight reparenting WM is required and that dependency must be recorded
set the 'window matches image size' preference to 'when opening images', which is the precondition named on the pull request
author the minimized trigger: maximize, enter fullscreen, leave fullscreen, read the window state
author the neighbouring legal check: the same round trip from a non maximized window must leave geometry unchanged
run three affected reproductions and three fixed controls

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the trigger is pure key delivery into a QWidget and the observable is whether the widget keeps servicing its event loop. Typing the degree character followed by a digit sends the parser into an infinite loop, so the main window stops repainting and stops answering accessibility queries. Detecting it means asserting liveness of a real QWidget tree after a keystroke: deliver the keys, then require the display label to report a value within a bound. That is the strongest possible check that the adapter's key path reaches the widget and that its observation path is a live query rather than a cached snapshot. Fourth application in the set and the only one whose failure mode is a hang

blockers.detail: there is no reproit-field-linux-qt-widgets worker image yet. Two are needed, not one: a Qt5 Widgets image for keepassxc and qView, and a Qt6 plus KF6 image for kcalc. Neither was built here because this gate was research only and the Docker daemon was in use by other work
no candidate was compiled at either revision, so every buildQualified claim is absent by construction. All five selected defects carry the compile step in remaining

the qView defect is a maximize and fullscreen state transition. A bare Xvfb has no window manager, so setWindowState may not produce the state the defect depends on. Whether a reparenting WM must join the image, and which one, is unverified

the kcalc defect reproduces as an event loop freeze. The evidence shape used by electron-linux records a compared observable, not a liveness timeout, so the benchmark record needs a decision on how a hang is expressed before this defect can be executed
